name: ibm_aml_sample

spec.name: ibm_aml_sample
spec.label_definition: positive = the account appears on at least one row flagged is_suspicious. Every row in this extract is flagged, so every entity is positive
notes: This is the laundering-pattern extract of IBM's synthetic AML data. It contains no negative class and cannot train or evaluate a classifier.
Amounts span 15 currencies and are not FX-converted.

data.identity_representation: entity ids are the source dataset's account/name identifiers as loaded; no resolution or merging was applied by the audit

labels.definition: positive = the account appears on at least one row flagged is_suspicious. Every row in this extract is flagged, so every entity is positive
labels.cross_validation_note: every entity is positive; there is no negative class to learn against
labels.prospective_or_retrospective: retrospective: the flag was attached after the behaviour it describes was complete, so a feature computed over an entity's whole history sees the period the label was assigned from

structural_triviality.note: the population is single-class; no ranking metric is defined and no triviality statement can be made

stratified_kfold.note: 3183 positives over 4 folds leaves about 795 per test partition

time_forward_holdout.note: a forward cut leaves enough positives in the later partition

component_grouped_kfold.note: components are the grouping unit; usable whenever k-fold is, but fold sizes follow the component-size distribution and can be very uneven

reason: every entity is positive; there is no negative class, so no classifier can be trained or evaluated
recommended_use: none until a negative population is obtained
limitations: SYNTHETIC: rows were generated, not observed. No result on this dataset is evidence about real-world detection performance.
